title: Treatment and Rehabilitation of a Patient with Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder-Induced Complete Spinal Cord Injury Following COVID-19 Vaccination: A Case Report
case_prompt: A 52-year-old woman presented to the emergency department 10 days after receiving a third dose of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine with pain in both eyes, numbness in both legs, difficulty walking, and dysuria. She had no prior similar episodes or cognitive impairment. PCR tests were negative for SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and HIV. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated total protein at 101.3 mg/dL but was otherwise unremarkable. A T2-weighted spinal MRI revealed an intramedullary hyperintense lesion extending from T2 to T12. On hospital day 2, muscle strength in both lower extremities deteriorated to the point that no voluntary movements were observed. Brain MRI demonstrated hyperintense lesions in the optic chiasm and optic nerve, and visual evoked potentials showed central conduction delay.
diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Multiple sclerosis was considered — “NMOSD and MS present with similar clinical manifestations and habitual relapses, complicating the diagnosis of NMOSD; however, some MS treatments can exacerbate NMOSD.” 2. Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis was considered — “It is crucial for NMOSD to be differentiated from acute disseminating encephalomyelitis, MS, the Guillain–Barre syndrome, and neuro-Behçet’s disease.” 3. Guillain–Barre syndrome was considered — “It is crucial for NMOSD to be differentiated from acute disseminating encephalomyelitis, MS, the Guillain–Barre syndrome, and neuro-Behçet’s disease.” 4. Neuro-Behçet’s disease was considered — “It is crucial for NMOSD to be differentiated from acute disseminating encephalomyelitis, MS, the Guillain–Barre syndrome, and neuro-Behçet’s disease.”
